design_rationale:
REVISION 4 - the counting basis of every month window is now fixed by policy (KB audit N-e).
Each of this task's three extended policies carries a temporal_basis block of the same shape as
the two base time eligibilities - clock frozen_time, anchor the day the account is worked,
relation not_before, unit calendar_months, an explicit counting_rule and an exclusive boundary -
and the counting rule stands as a sentence of each policy's own rule and of its baseline.rule, so
the computation document carries it: "A window of calendar months in this policy runs back from
the day the account is worked and never from the turn of a named month: an entry falls inside such
a window while fewer than that many whole months have gone by since the day it was booked, a whole
month going by only when the same day of the month comes round again, so an entry exactly that many
whole months old falls outside it, and an entry booked after the day the account is worked falls
outside it too." Every window phrase in every face - rule, baseline.rule, compute_basis and each
ladder tier - now reads "in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked"
or its two-, three- and twelve-month forms, so a factor document standing alone carries the basis
its own tier turns on. The wording was checked against the scoring harness before it was written:
an independent implementation of the sentence agreed with the harness on all 3,464 (day, window)
pairs swept across both worlds, including a 400-day sweep either side of each clock. On this
world the windows open on 2026-02-18 (one month), 2026-01-18 (two), 2025-12-18 (three) and
2025-03-18 (twelve), the clock standing at 2026-03-17.
Every scored value, whole baseline, factor sensitivity and edge-skip figure was re-derived on this
world after the change; all of them are unchanged, because the basis now written down is the one
the arithmetic already applied. The figures are listed in section 12.

WORKLOG - employee_meal_account_desk / task 0 (Theo Vandeleur, restricted payroll meal account)
REVISION 3 - reworked against audits/.../0.md and _difficulty.md `# revision_2`.

0. WHAT CHANGED IN REVISION 3, ITEM BY ITEM
N-2 (the value "settled from the account" never leaves the account): the reinstatement no longer
  sets the employee's stored value against the charges at all. Stored value is the employee's own
  spendable money and the charges awaiting recovery are met from pay; the rule now says so
  outright - "Nothing the employee holds as stored value is taken off the balance standing at
  reinstatement: stored value is spendable money of the employee's own, the charges awaiting
  recovery are met from pay, and the two are never set against each other by this restatement."
  The paydown remains what the plan asks the employee to pay in before the restriction is lifted
  (base meal_restriction_terms, as this difficulty's declared overwrite restates it: "A restriction
  is lifted once the employee has paid in at least the paydown worked out here"), and it stands to
  their credit as spendable value. meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance is redesigned around the one
  quantity that genuinely moves: the part the employer's dining programme picks up. Its result is
  balance standing less that pickup, the arrears fall by exactly that pickup, and the settlement row
  the tool books carries exactly that amount - so the formula, the field and the ledger row agree
  and no write claims a movement it does not make. The paydown still bears weight on the
  reinstatement, now through the uplift the employer's programme allows for the employee's own
  payment.
R2-F-1 (a proof sentence the ladder contradicts): every counterfactual in this dossier and in
  prerequisite_closure was recomputed by the Step 5 harness before it was written, and each names
  only the figures that run produced. The intermediates are quoted from the run's own binding dump,
  reproduced in section 12. In particular the third edge's proof now states the binding that
  actually moves - the uplift the employer's programme allows for the employee's own payment - and
  the figure the run gives.
N-1 (a factor labelled `parameter` while selecting a history window): the reinstatement's
  employer_pickup_base is declared `effect: method`, because its rungs choose which charges are
  summed (the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked, or none); its ladder carries
  `method` entries accordingly. The policy still declares 3 `parameter` and 1 `method` factors.
N-6 (a reference field emptied rather than repaired, and payroll-tendered guest meals with no
  accrual): this task's ledger now seeds the till transaction every accrual answers. Thirteen
  charge accruals each carry the pos_reference of the payroll-tendered meal they answer, and the two
  guest meals carry accruals of their own, so base meal_purchase_posted's trigger into
  meal_charge_accrued is honoured for every payroll-tendered row. The guest accruals are the meal
  less the guest surcharge printed against the plan, because the surcharge is not carried to payroll
  - meal_ext_reinstatement_paydown's rule now states that - which is why charging it in the paydown bills nothing twice.
N-3 (a baseline sentence with a dangling demonstrative): meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance's
  baseline.rule now defines the base and the share before it uses them, and every sentence of it is
  verbatim in the policy's rule.
CG-14, CG-8, CG-9: carried forward unchanged; CG-14 is the accepted runtime-layer known issue.

1. WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
The caller asks for one thing: his badge should charge lunch to his pay again. He names no recovery,
no paydown and no figure, and does not know what he owes. The agent must read out of the published
rules that the charges awaiting recovery must first stand net of the recovery entry owed for the
period his latest accrued charge belongs to, that his own paydown must then be paid in, and only
then what the account carries forward. Three multi-factor computations over a thirty-five row ledger
follow, three of their factors reading the employer's cafe programme and micro market at the site.

9. RULE <-> COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP
Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, branches, caps or rounds quotes its own
rule sentence in compute_basis. Reverse: "in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked" -> within_months=1 on
posted_date; "in the last two / three / twelve calendar months" -> within_months=2/3/12; "to date"
-> no window; "recovered on a semimonthly or a monthly cycle" -> F('payroll_cycle'); "meals of the
employee's own" -> transaction_code='meal_purchase'; "guest meals" -> transaction_code='guest_meal';
"an active micro market at the account's site" -> CFIELD('market','status'); "serves two or more
meal periods a day" -> CPARAM('cafe','meal_periods_served'); "the whole months between the day the
account was activated and the day its restriction began" -> MONTHS(F('activated_date'),
F('restriction_start_date')); "never read as less than nothing" -> MX(0.0, ...); "held to" ->
MN(...); "rounded to two decimal places" -> RND(..., 2).

14. REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION
Every write lands synchronously at frozen_time 2026-03-17 10:35:00 -04:00. Nothing waits on a pay run, a clearing, an
approval or a future date. Every question a real agent must ask has an answer in the persona; what
he owes is explicitly a matter for the record.
user_scenario:
Theo Vandeleur is forty-one, an instrument engineer at a research campus outside Boston, and he rings the workplace dining line late in the morning sounding more embarrassed than annoyed. He eats in the building cafe most working days and has always let the meals come off his pay; a couple of weeks ago the till stopped letting him do that, and this morning it refused again in front of half his team. That is how he opens: his badge used to charge lunch to his pay and now it will not, and what he wants out of this call is to get his badge charging to payroll again before the end of the week.

He gives his name, Theo Vandeleur, without being asked. When the desk needs more to find him he reads out his direct line, 6175340182, and then, turning the card over in his hand, the badge number printed on it, 45207318. His work address, theo.vandeleur@westvale-labs.com, and the postcode on his billing profile, 02142, he gives only if he is asked for something further; the site on the badge holder, CS-517, he reads out only when someone asks which building he eats in. He has no account reference numbers at all and says so plainly rather than inventing one.

He has not looked at what he owes, and he admits it. He knows he has been eating there most days and assumes it has mounted up, but he could not put a figure on it and would rather be told than guess. How the dining programme is funded, what the cafe contributes, how a pay packet is worked out - none of that means anything to him, and when the agent explains a rule he listens, says that is fine, and leaves it to them.

He is content for the desk to do whatever it needs to on its own side without checking with him line by line, and he says as much. What he will not do is read a card number down the phone. He does say outright that if he has to put money on it himself to get this sorted, he will, as long as somebody tells him exactly how much. When the agent hands him the means to make that payment and gives him a figure, he repeats the figure back and then makes the payment there and then for exactly that amount. If no figure is given to him he waits and asks what he is meant to pay, rather than choosing an amount himself.

He responds to what he is actually told. Once he hears that the account has been put back to normal and that lunch can go on his pay again, he thanks the agent, says he will try it at the counter in the morning and rings off. If he is told part way through that something is still outstanding, he says he would rather clear it now than have this happen again in a fortnight. If a figure he is read back does not match what he has just paid, he says that it does not look right to him and asks for it to be checked against the record - he never offers a number of his own to replace it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the dining profile of the employee on the line from the direct line he reads out, and read back the badge number, site, employer account code and profile details held on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the profile reference nothing else on this call can be located: every meal account, ledger and employer-programme lookup is keyed on it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record a passing identity check on the profile from the two details the caller states, the direct line and the badge number.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing may be quoted back about the account and no money may be moved on it until the caller is verified; the two details meet the desk's match threshold.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the employee's meal account and read the plan held, the state it stands in, the payroll cycle, the day the restriction began and the three running quantities.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan fixes every printed ceiling, share and threshold the three computations use; the state, the cycle and the restriction date decide the tier of the ceiling band, the recoverable window, the reinstatement share band and the value application basis.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the whole transaction ledger of the account: charges accrued, recoveries remitted, loads, the overdraft charges, the employee's own meals met from stored value and the guest meals tendered against payroll, each with its amount, day, transaction subtype, payroll period and tender.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every history aggregate of all three computations is reconciled from these rows - the accrual and recovery totals to date and over the one, two and three month windows, the load dates, the overdraft count, the employee's own meals and the guest meals.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's workplace cafe programme standing at the account's site: the service model held and the state the contract is in.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Two factors take their tier from it - the employer programme share of the period recovery, through the per-employee daily subsidy that service model publishes, and the employer pickup share of the reinstatement, through the number of meal periods it serves each day.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's unattended micro market at the account's site and the state it stands in.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The base the employer's programme picks up from at reinstatement is decided by whether that market stands active; without it the pickup falls to nothing and the restated figure is wrong.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk's payroll recovery write so the period's recovery can be remitted.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Remit the payroll period's recovery against the account, booking the recovery entry and taking the charges awaiting recovery down by it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The period recovery policy uniquely produces recovered_amount_usd; until this entry stands, the payroll period the most recent accrued charge carries has no recovery against it, which is what both later figures wait on.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.meal_account_id: The value is the reference of the employee's only meal account, read from the meal account lookup at action 2. The basis is the tool's own schema line, "the reference number of the employee meal account the recovery is remitted against; read it from the meal account lookup before this call". Uniqueness: the profile holds exactly one meal account, so the lookup returns one candidate.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.recovered_amount_usd: 83.85. The remittance is due now, because this policy's own rule fixes it as soon as the charges awaiting recovery stand above the plan's 200.00 restriction threshold, and they stand at 238.60 (303.45 accrued less 64.85 recovered). The account is recovered on a semimonthly cycle and the latest recovery was remitted 2026-02-06, 39 days before the clock and inside the 45-day recency window, so the recoverable balance is the charges of the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked, 273.45, less the 64.85 recovered in those months: 208.60. The employer's cafe programme at CS-517 stands active and publishes 7.25 per employee per service day, at or above the 7.00 strong support level, so it meets 7.25 for each of the 11 charges accrued in the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked = 79.75, leaving 128.85. The account stands restricted with 5 charges accrued in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, so the recovery ceiling is the uplifted share of the plan's 125.00 deduction ceiling = 200.00, which does not bite. Two overdraft charges stand in the last three months, so the deep deferral of 45.00 is taken off, giving 83.85, below the balance standing. Any agent reading the same ledger converges on 83.85.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.pay_period: 2026-03-P1. The basis is the rule sentence "The payroll period a remittance is made for is the period carried by the most recent charge accrued on the account." The most recent charge accrued is the 38.90 charge of 2026-03-13, whose pay_period is 2026-03-P1. Uniqueness: only one accrual is the most recent, so only one period can be named; 2026-02-P2, 2026-02-P1 and the earlier periods belong to earlier charges, and the format the schema fixes, YYYY-MM-P followed by one digit, admits no other spelling of it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the employee's own payment action and hand it over so he can pay the paydown from his card.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The second problem of the tree is the customer's own write; the agent may only hand it over, and the unlock changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The employee pays the paydown onto his own meal account from his card, booking the load entry and raising the stored value standing on the account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The reinstatement paydown policy uniquely produces paydown_amount_usd, and only the employee may make the payment; until the load entry stands, the stored value has not been raised by the paydown the plan calls for.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.meal_account_id: The value is the reference of the employee's only meal account, read out to him by the desk from the meal account lookup at action 2. The basis is the tool's own schema line, "the reference number of your workplace meal account, as the dining services desk reads it out to you before you make the payment". Uniqueness: the profile holds one meal account, so there is one candidate.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.paydown_amount_usd: 134.16. The account has stood restricted 21 days, longer than twice the 10 grace days printed against the plan, and a recovery was remitted on it this calendar month, so the measured balance is the last three months' charges 273.45 less the recoveries remitted in those months 148.70 = 124.75. It has stood restricted longer than the 10 grace days and 8 charges have been accrued in the two calendar months running back from the day the account is worked, so the required share is the escalated 75 per cent: 124.75 x 75 per cent = 93.56 rounded at that step. Stored value of 18.40 is at least the plan's 5.00 minimum load and the last load was 56 days ago, inside the 90-day recent load window, so the whole 18.40 is credited, leaving 75.16. That 18.40 is below the plan's 30.00 single transaction ceiling and 6 meals of his own were rung in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, so the plan's 25.00 reload amount at the heavy use multiple, 50.00, is added. The plan allows guest meals and 2 were rung in the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked, whose 4.50 surcharge each was not carried to payroll, so 9.00 is added. 75.16 + 50.00 + 9.00 = 134.16, above the 5.00 minimum load and below the 150.00 maximum. Any agent reconciling the same ledger converges on 134.16.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk's reinstatement write so the restriction can be taken off and the carried charges restated.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair for the root problem; it changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Take the spending restriction off the account, putting it back into the active state with the day the restriction began cleared, and set the charges awaiting payroll recovery to the restated figure.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The restriction lift policy uniquely produces arrears_carried_usd, and this write is the terminal state the caller asked for: payroll tender working again at the till.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.meal_account_id: The value is the reference of the employee's only meal account, read from the meal account lookup at action 2. The basis is the tool's own schema line, "the reference number of the employee meal account whose restriction is being taken off; read it from the meal account lookup before this call". Uniqueness: one profile, one meal account, one restriction standing.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.arrears_carried_usd: 123.71. After the period recovery the balance standing is 303.45 accrued less 148.70 recovered = 154.75. Nothing the employee holds as stored value is set against it. The employer holds an active micro market at CS-517 and 5 charges were accrued in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, so the base the employer's programme picks up from is that month's charges, 124.15. The employer's cafe programme at the same site stands active and serves two meal periods a day, so the standing share is the broad 12 per cent; value was paid onto the account this calendar month and the restriction has stood 21 days, longer than the plan's 10 grace days, so the matched paydown uplift of 8 is allowed; and 34 whole months stand between the day the account was activated and the day its restriction began, more than the 24-month long service term, with 5 charges in the month, so the long service uplift of 5 is allowed. 124.15 at 25 per cent is 31.04, and 154.75 - 31.04 = 123.71. Any agent working the same ledger converges on 123.71.

edges.condition: the payroll period carried by the account's most recent accrued charge has its own recovery entry on the ledger, so the charges awaiting recovery stand net of it
edges.policy_source: The paydown the employee is asked for is not worked out before the charges awaiting recovery stand net of the recovery entry owed for the payroll period the account's most recent accrued charge carries.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The account's most recent accrued charge is the 26.50 charge of 2026-03-13, which carries pay_period 2026-03-P1, and the only recovery entries on the ledger are remitted for 2025-12-P2 and 2026-01-P2; nothing on the ledger carries 2026-03-P1, so the charges awaiting recovery are not net of the recovery that period owes.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The recovery entry booked at action 7 carries pay_period 2026-03-P1 - the very period the most recent accrued charge carries - so the condition holds immediately after it; the recomputed run gives recoveries_remitted_1m 83.85 and measured_balance_usd 124.75 in place of the 238.60 the opening world would give.

edges.condition: the payroll period the account's latest accrued charge belongs to carries its own recovery entry on the ledger, so the charges awaiting recovery stand net of it
edges.policy_source: The charges an account carries forward at reinstatement are fixed only after the charges awaiting recovery stand net of the recovery entry due for the payroll period the account's latest accrued charge belongs to.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The same period, 2026-03-P1, carries no recovery entry at the opening: the balance standing is the whole 238.60 rather than a figure net of what that period owes.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The recovery entry booked at action 7 for 2026-03-P1 closes it; the recomputed run gives balance_standing_usd 154.75 in place of 238.60, and the charges carried forward are worked out on that figure.

edges.condition: a load entry for the paydown stands on the account's ledger and the stored value standing has risen by it
edges.policy_source: The charges carried forward are worked out only once the stored value standing on the account has been raised by the paydown the plan calls for.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: No load has been made on the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked: the latest load entry is dated 2026-01-20 and the stored value standing is 18.40, so value_loaded_1m is 0.00 and the uplift the employer's programme allows for the employee's own payment is nothing.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the employee pays 134.16 in at action 9 the recomputed run gives value_loaded_1m 134.16 and paydown_uplift_pct 8 in place of 0, so the employer's pickup rises from 21.11 to 31.04 and the charges carried forward fall from 133.64 to 123.71.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three edges leave a total order: the paydown depends on the recovery and the reinstatement on both, so no pair of writes may be swapped and there are no parallel edges to reorder. The swap was run: with the paydown placed before the recovery it is worked out on the opening world and comes to 150.00 rather than 134.16, the recovery is unchanged at 83.85 because it reads no load rows, and the reinstatement figure coincides at 123.71, because the uplift the paydown unlocks is allowed on the fact of a payment rather than on its size. The terminal state still differs - the load entry carries 150.00 rather than 134.16 and the stored value standing ends at 168.40 rather than 152.56 - so the two orders are distinguishable and the order the prerequisite sentences state is the one gold takes.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the recovery and replaying the rest leaves the paydown at 150.00 instead of 134.16: recoveries_remitted_1m is 0.00, so the measured balance falls back on the twelve-month basis, 238.60 rather than 124.75, and the escalated share takes the figure to the plan's largest single load.
Skipping the recovery leaves balance_standing_usd at 238.60 rather than 154.75 while the employer's pickup is unchanged at 31.04, so the charges carried forward become 207.56 instead of 123.71.

Skipping the employee's paydown leaves value_loaded_1m at 0.00, so paydown_uplift_pct falls from 8 to 0 while standing_share_pct stays 12 and service_uplift_pct stays 5; the employer's pickup falls from 31.04 to 21.11 and the charges carried forward become 133.64 instead of 123.71.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario contains no mention of a payroll recovery, of a closed pay period, of arrears standing unrecovered, of a paydown or of any figure, and no hint that something must be sorted out first. Theo raises only the root problem - lunch should go on his pay again - and explicitly says he has not looked at what he owes and could not put a figure on it. His only contribution touching a prerequisite is passive and conditional: he will put money on the account himself if somebody tells him how much, which he says only in answer to being told, and he waits rather than guessing if no figure is given.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_payroll_recovery_c9e76aa9 books its ledger row and updates the arrears field from the arguments it is given; it reads no other problem's rows and raises nothing. load_arrears_paydown_ff1c695b books the load and raises the stored value whether or not any recovery has been remitted. lift_meal_account_restriction_a306574a flips the status and writes the figure it is handed whether or not a paydown stands on the ledger: an agent who calls it first still gets a receipt, and the only consequence is a different terminal hash. None of the three contains an eligibility test, a prerequisite test or a policy-based Error return.

factor_trace: recovery_ceiling_band (parameter): the account stands restricted and 5 charges were accrued in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked (18.20, 24.70, 27.85, 26.90, 26.50), so the first rung applies and the ceiling is the uplifted share of the plan's 125.00 deduction ceiling, 200.00 - which does not bite here.
